long_description.before:
RiskCube enables startups to close enterprise deals with top-rated insurance.

Mission: Building insurance products & services focused on lowering the protection gap for the innovation economy on a national and global scale. 

Today, we operate an insurance brokerage focused on startups. Through the brokerage, we see firsthand where traditional insurance products fail, from AI liability and autonomous systems to defense technology and new space risks.

We are now building proprietary risk models that can price risks even when little historical claims data exists. Our approach uses stochastic simulation, then applies traditional, explainable models to make the output transparent to underwriters and regulators.

This allows us to create new insurance and reinsurance products for emerging industries much faster than traditional carriers.

long_description.before:
Graphify is a Knowledge Graph control plane for enterprise software. The open-source tool has 116K+ GitHub stars and 6.5M+ downloads, and is used in production by engineers at Shopify, Datadog, JP Morgan, American Express, Harvey, Automation Anywhere, and Vanguard.

On top of that graph, our enterprise layer reviews every pull request and formally verifies each code change: it proves the new behavior matches the old, or hands back the exact input that breaks it. That makes it built for the changes teams fear most, like refactors, framework upgrades, and large-scale migrations, where you need proof that nothing broke, not a guess.

The graph updates itself as the code changes and keeps context instead of forgetting it, so your whole team and their coding agents work from one shared, always-current view of the codebase instead of a thousand private threads.

It runs entirely inside your perimeter, fully air-gapped on-premise or self-hosted in your own cloud, so no code or data ever leaves your environment.

long_description.before:
TrueMile is a trucking company run by AI agents. Drivers who own their trucks join our company and earn 30% more profit, while agents run our back office so one person can now manage 9x the amount of trucks. 

Companies that ship goods don't sign contracts with one-truck businesses. So these drivers contact brokers one by one, taking jobs as they become available. That's the trap. A job that looks great can strand you in a city where the next jobs pay less. Our AI negotiates brokers across 10 markets at once to weigh profit across the whole week, not just one job at a time.

Trucking is insanely hard to scale because more trucks always meant hiring more people. Now we're finally able to scale truck count without spending time, resources, and dollars hiring for the back-office.

Founder / CEO Harpreet is a data scientist who has generated over $7.2M in freight revenue. 

For owner-operators and freight partnerships: harpreet@truemile.ai

long_description.before:
Agent Relay lets software teams' AI coding agents message each other directly, so people stop copy/pasting between Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and their teammates' agents. A frontend agent can ask the backend agent what an API returns, two agents can sort out a merge conflict between themselves, and your agent can answer a colleague's agent while you sleep.
 
Agents connect wherever they run: terminals, desktop apps, phones, laptops, cloud boxes, or a Mac mini across the world. Every session goes into shared, searchable history, so decisions don't get stuck in one person's chat. You can even let a customer's agent debug with yours. Setup takes about 5 minutes: give your agent the link and it installs itself. Use our hosted version free, or self-host the open-source version

The drug development pipeline is built around humans. Other AI biotech companies build automation around the established infrastructure. Halmos Labs rebuilds the infrastructure around automation. The central bottleneck is access to experiments. Halmos Labs' platform physicalvalidation.com offers a direct way to execute experiments in biolabs across the globe in days rather than weeks, managing risks and quality control. For every completed run, the platform builds tacit knowledge enabling faster and cheaper sourcing, and quality assurances. 

Using physicalvalidation.com, Halmos research agent is continuously designing drugs and has so far designed and tested a new mRNA cancer vaccine and a new antibiotic.
long_description.after:
AI can create new drugs and design experiments. They are limited by physical validation. 

physicalvalidation.com by Halmos Labs offers an API to execute any experiment. PhysicalValidation uses compounding knowledge and an experimental design AI to coordinate experiments through contracted labs faster and cheaper. 

Connecting physicalvalidation.com, Codex has designed and tested a new antibiotic without human intervention.

long_description.before:
Telamont catches contractual, technical and code-compliance risks in construction documents and gives teams the system to act on them before they become costly rework or disputes.

Construction projects lose money in the gap between what the documents say and what gets built. One missed discrepancy between the specs, drawings, geotechnical study and code can become a seven-figure claim eighteen months later.

Telamont connects to where your documents live and pulls in every file and revision as it lands, continuously building a complete picture of the project. Every page is checked against the rest of the project, so risks are flagged as soon as they appear. Instead of reviewing documents, teams act on flagged risks, tracking each from detection to resolution while managing exposure and pursuing recovery opportunities across every project.

long_description.before: Shire is an AI floor manager for full-service restaurants, running on the cameras they already have. It sees what a great manager sees: a guest ready to order, a table waiting on the check, a four-top that needs clearing, a server that is double booked. Then it acts, alerting staff in the moment and seating each new party with the server who has room. A POS only knows what gets typed into it. Shire knows what is happening in the room, so wait-time quotes, staffing, and pricing run on real turn times.
long_description.after:
Shire is building the operating system for self-driving restaurants.

Shire connects to restaurants' existing cameras to understand what's happening in real time. It sees what a great manager sees: guests ready to order, tables waiting to be cleared, and servers getting overwhelmed. Then it acts, directing staff, balancing workloads, and optimizing seating.

Shire is also the POS, combining payments and real-time restaurant operations with AI agents that handle the work managers do behind the scenes: scheduling staff, managing inventory, ordering supplies and analyzing each shift to improve the next.

Our goal is to automate everything in a restaurant except hospitality.

US workers' compensation paid out $64.1 billion in 2023. Personal injury, malpractice, and other insurance claims add billions more. Behind every one of these claims sit thousands of pages of medical records, and a clinician spends hours or days reading them to reconstruct what happened to the patient.

Elithia is building agents to do this work.

Our agents reconstruct patient histories, reason across conflicting evidence, and produce defensible analyses, with every finding cited to the original record.

We've sold to physician expert witnesses and medical-legal firms, turning thousands of pages into court-ready chronologies an expert can verify in minutes. Next: TPAs and insurers, where the same review sits behind every injury claim.

long_description.before:
Ageospatial helps organizations value the risk on their physical assets (properties, land, infrastructure) remotely using satellite imagery.

97% of commercial properties are never physically inspected because it's too slow and expensive. So insurers price risk based on what the client or broker tells them, and about half the time at least one of those records is wrong. The result is mispricing, fraud, and an estimated $36B in premium leakage every year in the US alone, which gets exposed the moment a disaster hits.

Upload a list of addresses and their GeoAI reads satellite and street-level imagery, maps, real-time data, public records and the insurer's own data to determine what's really there, which natural and human hazards surround it, what changed over time, and which properties are worth inspecting. Each property becomes a living record that underwriting, claims and pricing teams can trace from past to present. Ageospatial deploys inside carriers and MGAs as an AI-native service, so insurers get outcomes delivered.
long_description.after:
Ageospatial helps organizations value the risk on their physical assets (properties, land, infrastructure) remotely using geospatial AI. Some of the largest Banks and Insurance companies use our Geospatial AI Operating System.

insurers price buildings they’ve never seen. banks lend money on land they may never visit. so we take a look using geospatial data.

give us an address or a list of properties. our AI checks satellite images, street photos and public records alongside the customer’s own files. we put what we find in one operating system, with the source behind each finding.

an underwriter can see what a building is used for, what’s on its roof and whether it sits in a flood zone before deciding what premium to charge. a bank can use the same product to check whether a farmer planted the crop it financed, on the land it financed. one insurance company told us they found in seconds what would have taken them hours to look up by hand.
